units.text: This tutorial walks through a blue-green release of `orders-api`, a fictional web service, from a fresh build to a cleaned-up environment.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service

units.text: It assumes you already run the service behind a load balancer.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service

units.text: You keep two identical production environments, called blue and green.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › How blue-green works

units.text: One of them serves all live traffic while the other sits idle; you deploy the new version to the idle one, test it there, and then move traffic over in one step.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › How blue-green works

units.text: Because the old environment is still running, going back is the same one-step switch.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › How blue-green works

units.text: The cost is running twice the infrastructure during a release, which is why the idle environment is scaled down between releases.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › How blue-green works

units.text: You need the following in place before the first release:
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start

units.text: Two identical environments, `orders-blue` and `orders-green`, with the same instance count, instance size and configuration.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start

units.text: A health endpoint, `GET /healthz`, that returns `200` only when the service can reach its database and its queue.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start

units.text: Database migrations that are backward compatible, so the old version keeps working against the new schema. This is a hard requirement: both versions share one database, and a rollback does not undo a migration.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start

units.text: Access to the load balancer's listener rules, because the switch is a change to which target group the listener forwards to.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start

units.text: A dashboard or query that shows the 5xx error rate per environment, so you can tell green's errors from blue's.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start

units.text: If any migration is not backward compatible, do not use this procedure; split the migration into an additive release first and a cleanup release later.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start

units.text: In this walkthrough blue is live and green is idle.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps

units.text: **Deploy to the idle environment.** Deploy version `2.8.0` to `orders-green`, using the same build artifact that passed staging rather than a fresh build. Expected result: all green instances report the new version, and blue still serves 100% of traffic.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps

units.text: **Run the migrations.** Apply the database migrations from the new release, once, from a single job rather than from every green instance at startup. Expected result: the migration job exits with code 0, and blue keeps serving requests without new errors, which confirms the change is backward compatible.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps

units.text: **Check health on green.** Poll the health endpoint on every green instance until all of them return `200`. If any instance is still failing health checks after 10 minutes, stop here and roll back: tear down green and leave blue serving traffic. Nothing has been switched yet, so customers are unaffected.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps

units.text: **Smoke-test green.** Send the smoke-test suite to green's internal address. Expected result: all smoke tests pass. If one fails, treat it like a failed health check and stop.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps

units.text: **Switch traffic.** Point the listener at the green target group:
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps

units.text:
aws elbv2 modify-listener \
  --listener-arn "$ORDERS_LISTENER_ARN" \
  --default-actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn="$GREEN_TG_ARN"
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps

units.text: Expected result: within about 30 seconds, new requests are served by green, and blue receives no new connections.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps

units.text: **Watch the error rate.** Observe the 5xx error rate on green for 15 minutes after the switch. If the error rate rises above 2% at any point in that window, switch back: run the same command with `$BLUE_TG_ARN`, which returns all traffic to blue within about 30 seconds. If it stays at or below 2%, continue.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps

units.text: **Keep blue as a standby.** Leave blue running, unchanged, for 24 hours. It is your rollback target until then.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps

units.text: **Retire blue.** After 24 hours without a switch-back, scale blue down. Blue becomes the idle environment for the next release, with the roles reversed.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps

units.text: A rollback before step 5 is cheap, because customers never saw green.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong

units.text: A switch-back after step 5 is also fast, but requests that were in flight on green during the switch may fail and need a client retry.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong

units.text: Neither kind of rollback reverts the database, which is why the backward-compatible migration requirement matters.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong

units.text: Whichever way you roll back, record what failed before trying again, because a second attempt with the same build tends to fail the same way.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong

units.text: Do not run the next release's migrations while blue is still on standby.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong

units.text: If you do, the standby may no longer work against the schema, and the switch-back stops being a safe option.
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong

units.text: That's all there is to it. Happy deploying!
units.topic: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong
